summary: Replacement two-piece flip-top cap for a white lotion bottle with a snap-on (non-threaded) ribbed neck. The base snaps over the neck bead, seals with a short tube into the neck bore and dispenses through a 4 mm channel. The lid clips onto a 3 mm hinge pin on the base (C-clip, assembled after printing), plugs the channel with a short plug, and is held shut by a 45-degree snap latch on the thumb-tab side. PLA, no supports: base upside down, lid outer face down.

assumptions: A1: the neck is a snap-on neck, not threaded (the side profile shows vertical ribs and a bead, no helix). If it is threaded the whole sleeve design changes.
A2: rotation is not locked (no internal ribs to match the neck ribs): the cap is round and the channel is central, so orientation does not matter.
A4: the seal is a tube into the bore plus the deck pressing on the neck top; PLA is rigid, so it is splash-tight, not pressure-tight.
A5: rev 3: the shoulder lug sits inside the skirt (radius ~9-16 vs skirt bore 21.45), so the skirt extends to 0.5 above the shoulder (gap 6.7 measured) with no notch.
A3: the original white valve insert is not reused; the lid plug closes the open channel.
A7: the hinge is a clip-on pin hinge, not print-in-place (the base prints upside down, so a print-in-place lid would be under the bed). Both parts print without supports.
A8: hinge and latch sizes are design defaults; if the latch is too tight or too loose, only LATCH_DEPTH (D38) needs to change.
A9 (rev 5): PETG is the primary material (the user prints PETG). PLA is released with the same geometry, its own clearances (FITS) and a gentler latch (D38, D45 material_values).
